method: membrane-kv-runtime-relocate-probe 'failure' mode, extended this phase with 3 new retirement-specific cases.

invalid_layer.note: relocate(layer=99999) on a 30-layer model -- fails closed.

source_eq_destination.note: relocate to the layer's own current device -- allowed as a harmless redundant relocation (not rejected), layer stays valid.

duplicate_sequential_relocations.note: two sequential (not concurrent) relocations of the same layer -- both succeed, layer stays valid.

retire_without_pending.note: retire_layer_backing() called on a layer with NO deferred relocation pending -- correctly returns false, layer untouched.

retire_invalid_layer.note: retire_layer_backing(layer=99999) -- correctly returns false, layer untouched.

retire_duplicate_request.note: Real deferred relocation, retired once (succeeds), then retired again immediately (correctly fails closed -- nothing pending, does not double-free). A revealing sub-finding surfaced while building this case: deferring retirement on a layer's FIRST relocation (whose old backing is the SHARED construction-time bulk buffer) correctly refuses to ever retire that pending entry, since the scan always finds it still referenced by other layers -- this is safe (fails closed) but means a naive caller could accumulate permanently-unretirable pending entries if it only ever calls defer_retirement_for_research on first-time relocations. Documented as a known sharp edge of the RESEARCH-ONLY deferred-retirement escape hatch, not a concern for the validated real fix (immediate retirement + invalidate_graph_cache), which does not use deferred retirement at all.

requirement_met: original/current layer remains valid and usable in all 7 cases -- no half-rebound state, no double-free.
